title.narrative: Addressing the most urgent needs of vulnerable people affected by Hurricane Beryl in the Eastern Caribbean: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and Grenada

description.narrative: Hurricane Beryl, a record-breaking early Category 4 storm, caused widespread damage across multiple islands in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and Grenada, the most affected areas being Petite Martinique, Carriacou, Mayreau, Canaoun? and Union Island. In Union Island alone, preliminary data points at 90% of the homes being seriously damaged or destroyed. With key infrastructure seriously damaged, people have been evacuated and around 1,000 persons are being hosted in emergency shelter across the mainlands.With the CERF Rapid Response allocation, IOM will immediately kick-start the improvement of the emergency shelter benefitting including shelter repairs to 2,425 individuals. The interventions undertaken through this allocation will include: - Provide technical assistance to build emergency shelter management capacities and repair/upgrades to collective centers hosting 875 affected individuals, in coordination with partners and national Disaster Risk Management (DRM) agencies. - Provision of shelter repair kits to 500 affected households (estimated 1550 individuals), including distribution of tarpaulins, in addition to labour support and capacity building for persons who are unable to carry out repairs by themselves. The project will include strong community engagement and ensure the inclusion of and participation of vulnerable groups, applying also a robust gender equality, gender-based violence (GBV) risk mitigation, protection mainstreaming, and -sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) prevention perspectives in planned interventions. In line with the Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus, the proposed intervention includes an exit strategy aiming at setting the basis for future, mid-and long-term recovery programming.
